facts.text: Mission has one of the largest underdeveloped waterfronts in Western Canada, with 296 acres of land and over 3.5 km of frontage along the Fraser River.
facts.evidence: Mission is home to one of the largest underdeveloped waterfronts in Western Canada, encompassing 296 acres of land and over 3.5 km of frontage along the Fraser River.

facts.text: Mission's Waterfront Revitalization Master Plan charts the reactivation of underutilized land as a hub of activities, residences, industry and commerce.
facts.evidence: the Waterfront Revitalization Master Plan charting the reactivation of underutilized land as a vibrant hub of activities, residences, industry, and commerce.

facts.text: Mission's biggest employers are all government related, including the hospital, school board and correctional facility, and just nine businesses employ more than 100 people.
facts.evidence: The biggest employers are all government related, be it the hospital, school board, or correctional facility. There are just nine businesses that employ more than 100 people.

facts.text: Mission turns away many industrial inquiries because it lacks the flat land those businesses want.
facts.evidence: the main challenge Mission faces is a lack of available land, as it has to turn away many industrial inquiries because it doesn't have the flat land they are wanting.

overview: Mission had 41,519 residents in the 2021 Census, up 7.7 percent from 38,554 in 2016, in 14,098 occupied homes spread over 226.98 square kilometres. Low density and many single-family homes mean customers often drive to shop and compare options across the Fraser Valley.

Government employers such as the hospital, schools and corrections lead local employment, while waterfront redevelopment points to future commercial growth. Small businesses compete mostly for family households and commuters.
